model.name: Site / Campus
model.purpose: Provide the format-neutral context an agent needs to identify, describe, govern and operate a site or campus: a bounded area of land (with associated subsurface, surface water and airspace) held under coordinated management control, inside which facilities, infrastructure, circulation and open space are operated as one unit.
model.scope_statement: WM-BLT-008 models the managed physical container itself - its identity, classification, spatial extent, composition, control, lifecycle, operating conditions, measurement boundary and evidence - and stops at the interfaces with contained facilities (WM-BLT-006), the containing settlement or place (WM-PLC-005 / WM-PLC-002), the legal land unit, and the parties that own or operate it. Facilities, parcels, organisations, permits and individual assets are referenced by identifier, never re-modelled here. The model is projection-independent: IFC, CityGML, GeoJSON, Markdown, Git, MCP and MongoDB are encodings of these semantics, not the semantics.
in_scope: Site identity, naming, coding and identifier crosswalks across authoritative registries and internal systems
Site typology and classification against governed schemes
Declared managed extent: what is inside the site, including discontiguous parts and third-party enclaves
Boundary geometry, coordinate reference system, elevation datum, vertical and subsurface extent
References to the land parcels and tenure instruments the site rests on
Containment of facilities (WM-BLT-006) and on-site infrastructure networks
Ground surface, landscape, open space, parking and laydown areas
Internal zones, precincts, development phases, circulation routes and control points
Ownership, operatorship, duty-holder accountability and delegation
Regulatory authorisations, permits and registry interests attached to the site
Physical access control, perimeter and site information sensitivity
Lifecycle states, boundary change events, split/merge and successor lineage
Operating hours, site rules, permit-to-work regimes and service provision
Natural hazard exposure, contamination and environmental constraints
Emergency preparedness, evacuation and muster arrangements
Site-level quantities, areas, occupancy and capacity
Energy, water, waste and greenhouse-gas reporting boundary and meter coverage
Site-scale monitoring platforms and observations
Site records, evidence, provenance and retention
Alignment and crosswalks to external schemas and operational systems
out_of_scope: Internal anatomy of a building or civil facility - storeys, spaces, rooms, systems and building elements (WM-BLT-006 and its children)
Legal land title, deeds, rights, restrictions and responsibilities as first-class legal objects (land administration sibling model, aligned to ISO 19152-1)
Settlement, administrative area and populated-place semantics (WM-PLC-005, WM-PLC-002)
Legal entity, organisation and person records for owners, operators, staff, visitors and contractors
Individual equipment and plant items, their maintenance history and work orders (asset register and maintenance sibling models)
Construction and capital project delivery processes, programmes and contracts
Lease, licence and other commercial agreement terms
Address and geocoding conceptual model - addresses are referenced, not defined here
Utility network topology, capacity modelling and operations beyond the site demarcation point
Sensor and actuator device specifications - observations are referenced through SOSA/SSN patterns
Environmental permit legal instruments as documents of record (authorisation sibling model)
Financial valuation, depreciation and real-estate investment accounting

boundary_notes.distinction: IFC 4.3 keeps IfcSite and IfcFacility as separate spatial structure elements: a facility is aggregated by IfcProject, IfcSite or another IfcFacility, and decomposes into IfcFacilityPart and IfcSpace. WM-BLT-008 therefore records the containment edge, the facility identifier and the site-side demarcation point, and never re-states facility-internal structure.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Land parcel / cadastral parcel (land administration sibling model)
boundary_notes.distinction: A cadastral parcel is a legal spatial unit with homogeneous property rights, identified by nationalCadastralReference and inspireId, and used primarily as a locator. A site is a management construct: it may span many parcels, occupy part of a parcel, or include parcels held under different tenure. IFC 4.3 deprecated IfcSite.LandTitleNumber, reinforcing that title belongs elsewhere. WM-BLT-008 references parcels; it does not model rights, restrictions or responsibilities.

A settlement is an administrative or populated-place concept; a site is an operational container under a single management regime. A site can straddle two settlements or lie wholly outside any populated place, so containment by settlement is a recorded relationship with its own evidence, not a derived truth.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Regulatory facility registry entries (e.g. EPA FRS facility site)
boundary_notes.distinction: EPA FRS clusters program-system records under a 12-digit Registry ID and treats the originating programs as source of truth. A regulatory facility site is a reporting unit that frequently does not align one-to-one with the managed site: one site may carry several FRS interests, and one FRS record may cover only part of a site. The crosswalk must be recorded with match confidence rather than assumed.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Reporting boundary constructs (ENERGY STAR property, GHG Protocol organizational boundary)
boundary_notes.distinction: EPA Portfolio Manager models a campus as a parent property with child properties and does not support nested campuses; GHG Protocol sets organizational boundaries by equity share or control. Both are accounting boundaries that can diverge from the physical managed extent. WM-BLT-008 records each reporting boundary as a distinct, dated view over the site, never as the site's definition.

On-site distribution is in scope only up to the demarcation point where responsibility passes to an external network operator. Network topology, hydraulic or electrical modelling and upstream operations sit in the utility network sibling model.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Asset management system (ISO 55001) and asset information model (ISO 19650)
boundary_notes.distinction: ISO 55001 governs the management system and ISO 19650 governs information containers and trigger events. WM-BLT-008 is neither: it is the subject those systems act upon. It records which management system and information requirements apply, and cites their identifiers, without absorbing their clauses.

sources.title: IfcSite - IFC 4.3.2 Documentation
sources.relevance: Normative definition of a site as a spatial structure element: RefLatitude, RefLongitude, RefElevation, CompositionType COMPLEX/ELEMENT/PARTIAL, aggregation of sites and facilities, and the deprecation of LandTitleNumber and SiteAddress as of IFC4.3.0.0.

sources.title: IfcFacility - IFC 4.3.2 Documentation
sources.relevance: Defines the site/facility boundary: subtypes IfcBuilding, IfcBridge, IfcRoad, IfcRailway, IfcMarineFacility; facilities are aggregated by IfcProject, IfcSite or another facility and decompose into IfcFacilityPart and IfcSpace.

sources.title: FRS Description - Facility Registry Service
sources.relevance: Authoritative example of master-system site identification: a 12-digit FRS Registry ID clustering records from roughly 90 program systems, with program systems as source of truth, a weekly geospatial best-pick process and a data steward network.

sources.title: D2.8.I.6 INSPIRE Data Specification on Cadastral Parcels - Technical Guidelines
sources.organization: European Commission - INSPIRE Maintenance and Implementation Group
sources.relevance: Normative attribute set for the land basis a site rests on: inspireId, geometry, nationalCadastralReference, label, areaValue, referencePoint, validFrom/validTo and beginLifespanVersion/endLifespanVersion, plus the statement that parcels serve mainly as locators for geo-information.

sources.title: Semantic Sensor Network Ontology (SSN/SOSA)
sources.relevance: Supplies the observation pattern for site monitoring: Platform, Sensor, Observation, FeatureOfInterest, ObservableProperty, and the normative separation of resultTime (when the activity completed) from phenomenonTime (when the result applies to the feature of interest).

sources.title: 29 CFR 1910.38 - Emergency action plans
sources.organization: United States Department of Labor - Occupational Safety and Health Administration
sources.version_or_date: 67 FR 67963, 7 November 2002; current text as published by OSHA
sources.relevance: Normative minimum content for site emergency preparedness: written plan (oral permitted for 10 or fewer employees), reporting procedures, evacuation type and exit route assignments, critical-operations staff, post-evacuation employee accounting, rescue and medical duties, named contacts, a maintained employee alarm system, and defined review triggers.

sources.title: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, Security and Privacy Controls for Information Systems and Organizations
sources.organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.relevance: Physical and Environmental Protection (PE) control family provides the normative pattern for site perimeter and access governance: physical access authorizations, enforcement at defined entry and exit points, access logging, visitor control and inventory of physical access devices.

sources.title: OGC City Geography Markup Language (CityGML) Part 1: Conceptual Model Standard
sources.relevance: Semantic model for 3D urban objects with a Core module plus thematic modules including CityObjectGroup, LandUse, Relief, Transportation, Vegetation and WaterBody; supplies grouping, level-of-detail and land-cover concepts for site-scale representation and its encoding-independent conceptual layer.

sources.title: ISO 55001:2024 Asset management - Asset management system - Requirements
sources.relevance: Requirements for scope of the asset management system, leadership and accountability, life-cycle planning and control of change, documented information, and performance evaluation - the governance frame within which a site is held and operated.

sources.title: ISO 19152-1:2024 Geographic information - Land Administration Domain Model (LADM) - Part 1: Generic conceptual model
sources.relevance: Defines party, basic administrative unit, rights/responsibilities/restrictions, spatial unit, source and versioned object - establishing that legal land units and tenure belong to a land administration model rather than to a managed-site model.

sources.title: How to Benchmark a Campus in Portfolio Manager
sources.organization: United States Environmental Protection Agency - ENERGY STAR
sources.version_or_date: Guide dated March 2024; landing page updated 2025-01-06
sources.relevance: Public-authority rules for multi-building campus accounting: parent property and child property structure, absence of nested campuses, campus-serving meters recorded at the parent and single-building meters at the child, and a restricted list of property types eligible for campus-level certification.

sources.title: ISO 19650-1:2018 Organization and digitization of information about buildings and civil engineering works, including building information modelling (BIM) - Information management using building information modelling - Part 1: Concepts and principles
sources.relevance: Supplies asset information requirements, the asset information model, information containers and the common data environment as the agreed source of information, together with the trigger-event pattern that drives site information updates through the operational phase.

sources.title: GHG Protocol Corporate Accounting and Reporting Standard
sources.organization: World Resources Institute and World Business Council for Sustainable Development
sources.relevance: Defines organizational boundaries (equity share and control approaches) and operational boundaries (scope 1, 2 and 3) covering seven greenhouse gases - the basis for treating a site emissions inventory as a consolidation view distinct from the physical site.

sources.title: ISO 41011:2024 Facility management - Vocabulary
sources.relevance: Governed vocabulary for facility management terms used in site operating models, service provision and demand organisation, superseding the 2017 first edition.

bundles.name: Identity, classification and managed extent
bundles.description: Establishes which site is being described, what kind of site it is, and the declared rule for what falls inside it.
bundles.rationale: Every downstream statement about a site is meaningless until the subject is pinned to a stable identifier and the inclusion rule for its managed extent is explicit. IFC gives the entity a formal spatial identity, EPA FRS shows the master-data reality of multiple competing site records, and EPA campus guidance shows that the inclusion rule is a deliberate decision rather than an observation.

bundles.description: Where the site is in measurable terms, what land it rests on, and how it meets the world at its edges.
bundles.rationale: Geometry without a declared coordinate reference system and vertical datum is unusable, and a site boundary is routinely distinct from the parcels beneath it. INSPIRE fixes the parcel attribute set and its locator role, CityGML supplies the encoding-independent geospatial conceptual layer, and IFC fixes the site reference point and elevation datum.

composition.purpose: Site / Campus specialises the generic place concept, inheriting spatial referencing and naming semantics while adding managed-container behaviour.
Records the settlement or populated place that spatially contains the site, as an evidenced relationship rather than a derived truth, since a site may straddle or fall outside settlement boundaries.
The site aggregates facility records; IFC 4.3 confirms a facility may be aggregated by a site and that facility-internal structure belongs to the facility.

composition.target: Land administration / property right sibling model (LADM-aligned)
composition.purpose: Supplies parcels, basic administrative units, parties and rights, responsibilities and restrictions that the site references but must not re-model.
Resolves owner, operator, duty holder, service provider and regulator references; site identity must never be conflated with the operating legal entity.
Supplies typed addresses for postal, delivery, emergency and registered purposes; IFC deprecated the site-embedded address attribute, reinforcing external ownership of addressing.

composition.target: Authorisation, permit and licence sibling model
composition.purpose: Holds permits, licences and consents as legal instruments; the site records only which authorisations apply, their validity and their operational conditions.

composition.target: Asset register and maintenance sibling model
composition.purpose: Holds individual plant and equipment items and their work history; the site provides the location and management context under ISO 55001 rather than the asset records themselves.
Owns external network topology and operations; the site records only on-site distribution and the demarcation point where responsibility transfers.
Supplies Platform, Sensor, Observation, FeatureOfInterest and the normative separation of phenomenon time from result time, reused rather than redefined by this model.
Supplies the versioned-object pattern with beginLifespanVersion and endLifespanVersion alongside real-world validFrom and validTo, keeping event time and record time distinct.
Alignment target for spatial structure, composition type and site reference geometry. Alignment only: LandTitleNumber and SiteAddress are deprecated in IFC 4.3 and are not carried forward.
Alignment target for encoding-independent geospatial representation, city object grouping, land use and relief at site scale.
Alignment target for parcel referencing and lifespan versioning attributes when operating in the European regulatory context.
Alignment target for management-system scope, accountability, life-cycle planning and control of change applied to the site as a managed object.
Alignment target for information containers, suitability status, the common data environment as agreed source of information, and the trigger-event update pattern.

composition.target: GHG Protocol Corporate Standard boundary rules
composition.purpose: Alignment target for organizational and operational boundary setting when a site emissions inventory is compiled.

Alignment target for regulatory site identification and crosswalk reconciliation in the United States context; the FRS Registry ID is a master-system identifier candidate, not a global site identifier.

owner_package_requirements: The adopting Dimension must name a single accountable owner for the site model package and a named deputy, consistent with ISO 55001 assignment of responsibility and authority.
The package must declare its scope boundary against WM-BLT-006, WM-PLC-005 and the land administration sibling model, and must not redefine elements owned by those models.
The package must publish its identifier policy, stating the master systems it recognises, its governed global identifier schemes and its fallback UUID or ULID generator.
The package must declare a validation rule set version and the common data environment that acts as the agreed source of information for site records.
The package must maintain a register of alignments and conformance claims, distinguishing evidenced conformance from declared alignment.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Use one stable namespace per adopting Dimension, with a path segment for the model (site) and never a path segment for storage format or interface. Identifiers minted by the Dimension are opaque and are never derived from names, addresses, coordinates or dates. External identifiers are carried in a namespaced crosswalk, never merged into the local identifier space. Namespace changes require a redirect and a recorded supersession, since retired site identifiers are never reassigned.
registry_links: vr.wm-blt-008 (this model) in the world-model record plane
WM-BLT-006 Facility as the contained-model registry entry
WM-PLC-002 Place and WM-PLC-005 Settlement as parent and containing registry entries
External registry references recorded per instance: national cadastral register, EPA Facility Registry Service, and any benchmarking scheme property registry

canonicalization_rules: Canonical form is the format-neutral logical record; JSON, YAML, Markdown, HTML, IFC, CityGML, Git objects and MongoDB documents are projections and never authoritative.
All timestamps are canonicalised to RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset or Z; local wall-clock times without offset are rejected at ingest.
Geometry is canonicalised to a single declared coordinate reference system per record, with the CRS identifier stored alongside; reprojected copies are derived artifacts.
Collections are ordered deterministically by identifier for hashing; ordering carries no semantics unless a rank attribute is present.
Absent values are represented as absent, never as empty strings, zero or a sentinel date; a value that is deliberately withheld is marked withheld with a reason.
patch_rules: Every change is expressed as an addressed patch against a specific record version, carrying both the event time and the record time.
Identifier fields are immutable; a correction to a primary identifier is a supersession event with predecessor and successor links, not an in-place edit.
Boundary geometry, lifecycle state and accountability changes require an authorising role reference on the patch and are rejected without one.
Patches to reported quantities within a closed reporting period are recorded as restatements with an explicit reason, not as silent overwrites.
Patches are append-only in the change log; the log is never rewritten, and rollbacks are expressed as compensating patches.
compatibility_rules: Adding an optional element or a new coded value is a minor change; removing an element, tightening cardinality or narrowing a code list is a breaking change.
Deprecated elements are retained and marked with their deprecating version and replacement, following the IFC precedent for LandTitleNumber and SiteAddress.
Consumers must ignore unknown elements rather than fail, and must not infer meaning from element ordering.
A crosswalk is versioned against both the source model version and the target schema version; a target schema upgrade invalidates the crosswalk until re-verified.
No conformance to an external standard is claimed without a cited test or certification artifact; otherwise the relationship is recorded as alignment only.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier issued by the system of record for the site, for example an EPA FRS Registry ID or a national cadastral reference held by the responsible authority.
Governed global identifier or IRI from a maintained scheme, for example an INSPIRE external object identifier or an IFC GlobalId, where a persistence and non-reallocation policy exists.
UUID or ULID minted by the adopting Dimension, used only where no higher-priority identifier exists and recorded with the justification for its use.
A date, a name, an address, a coordinate pair or a file path is never an identifier and must not be used as a key.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: All time values are recorded in RFC 3339 format with seconds precision and an explicit UTC offset or Z. Event time (when the thing happened in the world) and observation or ingestion time (when the system learned of it) are recorded as separate fields wherever they can differ, following the SOSA separation of phenomenon time from result time. Date-only values are used solely where the source itself is date-only and are labelled as such.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serial artifacts are named as <site-identifier>/<artifact-class>/<sequence-or-period>/<revision>, where sequence is monotonically increasing within the site and revision is issued by the producing party. Reporting artifacts substitute the RFC 3339 period start and end for sequence. Sequence numbers are never reused after retirement, and gaps are permitted and explained rather than backfilled.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Every artifact carries a content digest over its canonical form, the producing party, the approving role and the approval timestamp. Superseded revisions are retained with a link to their successor and are never deleted before the retention period expires. Redacted derivatives carry a reference to their parent digest and the identifier of the redaction profile applied, so that any published extract can be traced to a controlled original.

policies: Boundaries and containment are recorded as authored, evidenced decisions with an authorising role, never inferred from geometry alone; a facility whose footprint falls inside the boundary is not thereby part of the site.
Legal, regulatory and commercial constructs are referenced by identifier and never re-modelled inside the site record; the site model holds applicability, validity and operational consequence only.

No conformance to an external standard is asserted without cited evidence; unevidenced relationships are recorded as alignments and any conflict between standards is recorded rather than resolved silently.
Security-sensitive site information is classified before publication, and any externally shared derivative is produced through an approved redaction profile traceable to its controlled original.
Reporting boundaries are maintained as dated views over the site and are never allowed to overwrite or redefine the managed extent.

read: Read of non-sensitive site identity, classification, boundary and composition is available to any authenticated agent within the adopting Dimension.
Read of security-sensitive elements including perimeter detail, access authorisations, access logs and buried-service records requires an explicit named grant and is logged.
Read of a superseded revision requires the same or stronger grant as the current revision and returns the supersession link.
Bulk read and export require a declared purpose, and any export crossing a Dimension boundary is produced through an approved redaction profile.
create: Site records are created only through the register-site function, which enforces the identity priority rule and a duplicate check.
Containment edges to facilities are created only where the facility identifier resolves and no conflicting exclusive containment exists.
Observations are created only for sensors registered in the current monitoring plan and only with both phenomenon time and result time supplied.
Artifacts are created with a content digest, producing party and approval record; artifacts without provenance are rejected.
update: Identifier fields are immutable; changes are expressed as supersession with predecessor and successor links.
Boundary, lifecycle state, accountability and extent changes require an authorising role and supporting evidence artifacts.
Updates carry both event time and record time; an update supplying only one of the two is rejected where they can differ.
Updates within a closed reporting period are recorded as restatements with a stated reason and do not overwrite the locked period dataset.
delete: Logical deletion only: records are retired or superseded, never physically removed while within their retention period.
Physical disposal occurs only under the approved retention and disposal schedule, with a recorded disposal authorisation, action and timestamp.
Retired site identifiers are permanently reserved and are never reassigned to a different site.
Deletion is blocked while any active authorisation, unresolved regulatory obligation or open legal hold references the record.

roles.name: Site model owner
responsibilities: Owns the model package, its scope boundary and its versioning
Maintains the register of alignments and conformance claims

roles.name: Site data steward
responsibilities: Maintains identifier assignment, crosswalks and reconciliation against external registries
Adjudicates below-threshold matches and records unresolved conflicts
Monitors completeness and currency of site records

roles.name: Site operator or facility manager
responsibilities: Maintains managed extent, containment, zoning, operating model and service arrangements
Authorises physical access within delegated limits
Ensures emergency and permit-to-work arrangements are current

roles.name: Geospatial and survey authority
responsibilities: Approves boundary geometry, coordinate reference system and vertical datum declarations
Certifies positional accuracy and survey provenance
Validates divergence between the operational boundary and legal parcel lines

roles.name: Compliance and reporting officer
responsibilities: Maintains the authorisation register and regulatory registry interests
Defines and locks reporting boundaries and consolidation approaches
Owns restatements, assurance evidence and submission records

roles.name: Security and information classification authority
responsibilities: Classifies site information by sensitivity and approves redaction profiles
Governs access grants to security-sensitive elements and audits their use
Adjudicates conflicts between disclosure obligations and security restrictions

access.default_rule: Deny by default. Access is granted per scope to a named role for a stated purpose and a bounded period; grants at bundle scope do not cascade automatically to security-classified findings or artifacts within them.
exceptions: Emergency response override: designated emergency roles and external responders receive immediate read of emergency, hazard, muster and circulation findings during a declared incident, with the override logged and reviewed afterwards.

Mandatory disclosure: information subject to a statutory publication or access-on-request obligation is released through the approved channel even where the operator would prefer to withhold it, with any permitted exemption recorded.
Regulator access: an authority holding a registry interest in the site receives read of the findings within its remit without a per-request grant, scoped to that remit.

Security withholding: perimeter detail, access authorisations, access logs, buried-service records and security-zone geometry are withheld from general and bulk read even where the containing bundle is otherwise readable.
Legal hold: records under legal hold are readable to the holding authority and are exempt from scheduled disposal until the hold is lifted.
audit_requirements: Every read of a security-classified finding or artifact is logged with actor, scope, purpose, RFC 3339 timestamp and grant reference.
Every write is logged with actor, authorising role, event time, record time and the change log sequence number it produced.
Every export crossing a Dimension boundary is logged with the redaction profile applied and the digest of both the parent and the derivative.
Emergency overrides and mandatory-disclosure releases are reviewed within a defined period after the event and the review outcome is recorded.
Audit logs are append-only, retained under the retention and disposal schedule, and are themselves subject to access control.

required_fields: Access default rule and classification scheme
read_order: AGENTS.md - establishes name, type and the four resolving URLs before any other action
Specification URL - the format-neutral model semantics, scope, exclusions and boundary notes
Storage type URL - how the current projection encodes the model, whether JSON, YAML, Markdown, Git, MongoDB or an IFC or CityGML exchange
Interface URL - the available read and write operations, authentication and the access default rule
Processes URL - the governed functions, their preconditions, authorising roles and effects
Alignment and crosswalk register - target schema versions, mapping losses and any conflicts before attempting exchange
Validation rule set - the rules a record must satisfy before publication

coverage.claim: This model covers the identity, classification, spatial basis, composition, control, lifecycle, operating regime, resilience, measurement, evidence and interoperability surface of a managed site or campus, grounded in fourteen live sources, all primary, spanning nine independent organisations (buildingSMART International, US EPA, European Commission INSPIRE, W3C, US OSHA, NIST, OGC, ISO, and WRI/WBCSD). It is deliberately bounded: legal land units, facility internals, parties, permits as instruments, and individual assets are referenced, not re-modelled. It does not claim conformance to any cited standard, only declared alignment, and it does not claim completeness across all jurisdictions or site types.

checklist.notes: Identity priority, master-system identifiers, governed global identifiers, UUID/ULID fallback, naming, retirement and non-reassignment are covered by the site-identity-and-designation finding and artifact_rules.identity_priority, grounded in EPA FRS (SRC-003), INSPIRE inspireId (SRC-004) and IFC GlobalId semantics (SRC-001).

State vocabulary, transition authority and evidence, split/merge lineage and trigger events are covered, grounded in ISO 55001 control of change (SRC-009) and ISO 19650 trigger events (SRC-012). The specific state vocabulary itself is an adopter decision and is marked as such rather than asserted.

Containment to facilities, reference to settlement and place, parcel coverage, adjacency, connection points and third-party enclaves are covered, grounded in IFC aggregation rules (SRC-001, SRC-002) and INSPIRE parcel locator semantics (SRC-004).

RFC 3339 with explicit offset or Z is mandated; event time and record time are held separately, reinforced by the SOSA phenomenonTime/resultTime distinction (SRC-005) and INSPIRE validFrom/beginLifespanVersion pairing (SRC-004).

Producing party, inputs, method, approval and content digest are required for artifacts; survey provenance and register verification dates are explicit. Grounded in ISO 19650 information containers (SRC-012) and EPA FRS source-system precedence (SRC-003).

Owner, operator, duty holder and delegation are separated with effective dates, grounded in ISO 55001 (SRC-009) and the LADM party and basic-administrative-unit separation (SRC-010). Legal title itself is explicitly out of scope.

A validate-site-record function, declared rule set versioning, match thresholds, conformance-evidence questions and publication blocking on mandatory-rule failure are all present (SRC-012, SRC-004, SRC-003).
Deny-by-default with four scopes, five exception classes and five audit requirements, grounded in the NIST SP 800-53 PE control pattern (SRC-007) and the ISO 19650 common data environment (SRC-012).

Retention periods with triggers and legal basis, disposal authorisation, logical-only deletion, permanent identifier reservation and legal hold are covered (SRC-007, SRC-003, SRC-009). Specific statutory retention durations are jurisdiction-dependent and are deliberately not asserted.

Alignment declarations, mapping-loss notes, matching rules, deprecated-element handling and an explicit alignment-not-conformance policy are covered against IFC (SRC-001, SRC-002), CityGML (SRC-008), INSPIRE (SRC-004), FRS (SRC-003), ISO 19650 (SRC-012) and GHG Protocol (SRC-013).

Scheme-versioned classification, multi-classification precedence, IFC composition type and reclassification triggers are covered (SRC-001, SRC-008, SRC-014). No single universal site typology is asserted, because none was found in the primary sources.

Boundary geometry, CRS, vertical datum, positional accuracy, reference point and vertical or subsurface extent are covered (SRC-001, SRC-004, SRC-008). Three-dimensional site volumes are supported conceptually but their encoding is left to the projection.
Areas, occupancy, capacity, meter coverage, allocation and consolidation approach are covered with mandatory measurement basis and date (SRC-011, SRC-013, SRC-004).

Perimeter, access authorisation, logging, device inventory and information sensitivity are covered from NIST SP 800-53 PE controls (SRC-007), including the disclosure-versus-security conflict resolution path.

Written plan requirement, evacuation and exit route assignment, employee accounting, alarm system and review triggers are taken directly from 29 CFR 1910.38 (SRC-006). This is US-specific and is flagged under regional assumptions.

Valuation, rent, service charge and capital planning belong to real-estate and finance sibling models. No primary source reviewed places commercial terms within a managed-site container model, so no structure is proposed here.

IFC 4.3 introduces IfcMarineFacility (SRC-002) and CityGML has WaterBody (SRC-008), but no primary source reviewed defines a managed-site container for offshore platforms, underground mines or relocatable sites. The vertical-extent and water-body elements are provided as a partial accommodation and this remains an unresolved boundary.

known_omissions: No governed global location identifier scheme is prescribed. GS1 GLN was investigated as a candidate but gs1.org returned HTTP 403 to every fetch attempt, so no GLN allocation rule is cited or relied upon anywhere in this model.

Reference designation systems for construction works (the ISO/IEC 81346 series, including RDS-CW) would give a rigorous site-to-facility-to-system designation grammar, but the texts are paywalled and no free normative extract was obtainable, so no designation grammar is asserted.

Buried-service record quality is modelled as a coded confidence level without binding it to a specific quality-level standard, because no freely readable normative source for subsurface utility record quality levels was verified in this session.
Waste, water discharge and air emission permit content is referenced but not decomposed; the decomposition belongs to an authorisation sibling model that does not yet exist in the registry.
Site-level accessibility requirements are limited to a question about designated accessible routes. No accessibility standard was cited as primary, so no requirement structure is proposed.
Biodiversity net gain, ecological baseline and habitat accounting appear only as protected-feature constraints; they may warrant their own layer in jurisdictions where they are mandatory.
The ENERGY STAR campus rules were read from the EPA landing page and EPA-published summaries; the guide PDF itself was not machine-readable in this session, so clause-level wording is not quoted.
conflicts: IFC 4.3 deprecates IfcSite.LandTitleNumber and IfcSite.SiteAddress (SRC-001), while many operational systems and earlier IFC exchanges still populate them. This model treats title and address as external references and records the deprecation as an explicit import and export handling rule rather than carrying the attributes forward.

EPA Portfolio Manager supports only a two-level parent and child property structure with no nested campuses (SRC-011), whereas IFC permits recursive site decomposition through COMPLEX, ELEMENT and PARTIAL composition types (SRC-001). The model keeps physical composition recursive and treats the benchmarking structure as a separate, flatter reporting view.

A regulatory facility site in EPA FRS is a reporting unit clustered from roughly ninety program systems (SRC-003) and frequently does not align one-to-one with a managed site. The model records extent alignment and match confidence rather than assuming identity between the two.

GHG Protocol organizational boundaries set by equity share or control (SRC-013) can include facilities the site operator does not manage and exclude ones it does. The model therefore forbids a reporting boundary from redefining the managed extent.

LADM treats the spatial unit as the carrier of rights and defines land administration around basic administrative units (SRC-010), whereas a managed site is defined by operational control. Where the two diverge the model records both, and does not attempt to reconcile them into a single boundary.

OSHA 29 CFR 1910.38 (SRC-006) permits an oral emergency action plan for employers with ten or fewer employees, which conflicts with the general expectation elsewhere in this model that controlling arrangements exist as retained artifacts. The finding records the requirement basis explicitly rather than mandating a written artifact universally.
regional_assumptions: The emergency preparedness finding is grounded in United States federal OSHA regulation (SRC-006). Other jurisdictions impose different minimum content, review cycles and written-plan thresholds; the finding structure is intended to be jurisdiction-neutral but its specific elements are US-derived.

Regulatory site identification is grounded in the US EPA Facility Registry Service (SRC-003). Equivalent national registries exist elsewhere with different identifier structures, matching rules and authority models.

Parcel referencing is grounded in the INSPIRE Cadastral Parcels specification (SRC-004), which applies to European Union member states. Cadastral systems elsewhere differ in identifier structure, area authority and whether parcel geometry is legally definitive at all.

Campus benchmarking rules including the parent and child structure and the restricted list of campus-certifiable property types are US EPA ENERGY STAR rules (SRC-011) and do not generalise to other benchmarking schemes.

The physical access control pattern follows NIST SP 800-53 (SRC-007), a US federal control catalogue. Organisations operating under ISO/IEC 27001 Annex A or sector-specific regimes will map to equivalent but differently structured controls.
Coordinate reference systems, vertical datums and land-cover classifications are all jurisdiction-specific; the model requires that each be declared and never assumes a default.
adversarial_checks: Counterexample sought for site-facility separation: IFC 4.3 permits a facility to be aggregated directly by IfcProject without an intervening site (SRC-002), so a site is not universally required. The model therefore treats containment of a facility by a site as a recorded relationship with its own evidence rather than a structural necessity, and does not require every facility to have a parent site.

Counterexample sought for contiguity: EPA campus guidance and real portfolio practice both include discontiguous holdings managed as one unit. The managed-extent finding therefore makes contiguity an explicit recorded flag with a federation justification, rather than assuming a single connected polygon (SRC-011).

Attractive but unsupported structure rejected: a universal site typology (industrial, campus, port, depot and so on) was drafted and then rejected, because no reviewed primary source publishes a governed cross-domain site classification. Classification is instead modelled as scheme-versioned assignments with a precedence rule, and the absence of a canonical scheme is recorded in the checklist.

Attractive but unsupported structure rejected: a site-owned tenure and rights sub-model was drafted and removed. LADM (SRC-010) and INSPIRE (SRC-004) place rights, restrictions and responsibilities with the land administration domain, and IFC 4.3 deprecated its own land-title attribute (SRC-001). Duplicating it here would have created two competing sources of legal truth.

Boundary stress test between site and reporting view: because both EPA Portfolio Manager (SRC-011) and GHG Protocol (SRC-013) produce site-shaped boundaries that diverge from physical management, a policy was added forbidding a reporting boundary from redefining the managed extent. Without it an agent would silently corrupt the site definition when compiling a return.

Identity stress test: a date, a name, an address and a coordinate pair were each tested as identifier candidates and rejected. FRS demonstrates that names and addresses are exactly the attributes that fail to resolve duplicate site records across roughly ninety systems (SRC-003), which is why match confidence, not attribute equality, governs reconciliation.

Sourcing stress test: four intended sources could not be read live in this session (gs1.org and iso.org return HTTP 403, ecfr.gov redirects off-host, and the ENERGY STAR campus PDF is not machine-readable). Every claim that would have depended on GS1 GLN was removed rather than asserted from memory; ISO catalogue entries are cited for title, edition and scope only, never for clause-level text; and OSHA's own hosted text was used in place of eCFR.
